sanskrit: रजो रागात्मकं विद्धि तृष्णासङ्गसमुद्भवम् । तन्निबध्नाति कौन्तेय कर्मसङ्गेन देहिनम् ॥
hindiTranslation: हे कुन्तीनन्दन  तृष्णा और आसक्तिको पैदा करनेवाले रजोगुणको तुम रागस्वरूप समझो ।  वह कर्मोंकी आसक्तिसे शरीरधारीको बाँधता है ॥
englishTranslation: Know rajas as passion-born, born of craving and attachment. It binds the embodied being through attachment to action, O son of Kunti.
essence: Craving turns action into a chain.
speaker: Krishna
simpleMeaning: Restless desire and attachment create rajas. That force traps a person by making them cling to action and its rewards.
simpleInsight: You can see how craving quietly turns action into bondage.
detailedMeaning: Arjuna still stands frozen while Krishna explains the three forces that shape human conduct. After describing sattva, Krishna now names rajas: the force of craving and attachment that ties the embodied person to restless doing.
modernRelevance: A shopkeeper who keeps rearranging stock and chasing one more sale, even after closing, may call it drive. Krishna would call it rajas, craving that binds a person through attachment to action.
translationLiteral: रजः (rajas) / रागात्मकम् (of the nature of passion) / विद्धि (know) / तृष्णा (craving) / सङ्ग (attachment) / समुद्भवम् (born from) / तत् (that) / निबध्नाति (binds) / कौन्तेय (O son of Kunti) / कर्मसङ्गेन (through attachment to action) / देहिनम् (the embodied being)
insight: Rajas is born of craving, and it ties a person to the restless need to keep doing.
